title: Parameter Estimation from Amplitude Collapse in Correlated Matter-Wave Interference
summary: Operating matter-wave interferometers as quantum detectors for fundamental physics or inertial sensors with unprecedented accuracies relies on noise rejection, often implemented by correlating multiple sensors. They can be spatially separated (gradiometry or gravitational-wave detection) or consist of different internal states (magnetometry or quantum clock interferometry), with a signal-amplitude modulation serving as a signature of a differential phase.
